voiceover:
[curious] This social media tool has quietly made over $1M in verified revenue.

Stay till the end, because the smartest move here isn't the AI.

It's called Marky. You add your website, and it writes a month of on-brand posts, designs the images, and publishes them to 7 platforms. Small businesses and agencies pay for it.

[confident] These numbers are verified on TrustMRR through Stripe. $22K a month in recurring revenue, 476 active subscriptions, about $17K in the last 30 days, and $1M all-time. All since July 2023.

How did it grow? Here's what's visible. It's bootstrapped, it sold a lifetime deal on AppSumo, and the founder posts launches and customer wins on LinkedIn. There's also a Pro plan at $229 a month with a white-label portal, so agencies can resell it.

[serious] Honest catch: revenue isn't profit, the category is crowded, and TrustMRR lists Marky for sale at $495K.

[whispers] Now the move. Marky sells the finished output, not the tool. Their pitch is that it designs the image, not just the caption. People don't want a scheduler, they want the posting done. And every plan starts with 30 free posts, no credit card.

[playful] So steal that: sell the result, and sell to agencies too. Would you build this or buy it?

Send this to the friend who keeps saying social media tools are too crowded to enter.

Hack saved?

topic: Business breakdown: Marky — A tool for self-publishing authors to manage their social media.

pick.topic: Business breakdown: Marky — A tool for self-publishing authors to manage their social media.
pick.angle: A tool for self-publishing authors, a niche most founders ignore, has crossed $1M in verified revenue

research.what_it_does: An AI social media manager. You add your website, and it writes a month of on-brand posts, designs the images, and schedules and publishes them to 7 platforms: Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, X, Google Business Profile, TikTok and Pinterest (about page).
research.who_pays: Small businesses and agencies. The Pro plan includes a white-label portal so agencies can resell Marky under their own brand.
research.pricing: Official pricing page: 'Get your first 30 posts free', no credit card needed. Solo $39/mo (1 workspace, 3 channels, 1 user). Growth $79/mo (5 channels, unlimited users, reputation management), marked 'Most Popular'. Pro $229/mo (8 channels, unlimited users, whitelabeled portal). Extra channels cost +$7/mo, and extra workspaces on Growth cost +$25/mo. The page's meta description says '$19/month billed annually' on the yearly toggle.
growth: AppSumo lifetime deal: Marky is sold on AppSumo, and AppSumo's own listing says it is bootstrapped and based in Austin, TX (appsumo.com/products/marky). Third-party reviewers (daveswift.com, sumolingers Substack) say AppSumo named it a 'Tool of the Year' for social media management in 2024. The Substack says the Tools of the Year deals returned until Dec 30. The review says these deals run only five days. I found no first-party statement from AppSumo or Marky on how many customers this brought in.

Founder-led content on LinkedIn: Josiah Coad posts feature launches ('Just launched a new feature to upload your own images'), customer wins and build-in-public notes. The Marky company LinkedIn page also posts, including agency-focused content ('agencies are scaling to hundreds of clients with Marky').
Agency/white-label angle: the Pro plan and the LinkedIn posts both target agencies that resell Marky to their own clients.

Founder interview (Momentum91 podcast): Coad describes how to get a first customer by acting like a consultant, and says that to scale you move from users knowing you first to users knowing the software first. The page summary says he grew MyMarky.ai from a one-person operation to a 12-person team. The page gives no date for that, and the episode is roughly 2 years old.
SEO comparison pages: Marky's own site runs pages such as 'Best AI Social Media Post Generator (2026): Honest Comparison', which compares it with Buffer and SocialBee.
Marketing channels listed on TrustMRR (not independently verified): Facebook, Meta Ads, word of mouth, influencers.
founder_story: Josiah Coad is listed on LinkedIn as 'Ex-Facebook/Tesla Software Engineer | Founder/CEO Marky'. Third-party profile sites (RocketReach, Success.ai) say he was at Tesla and John Deere before Marky. These aggregator sites are lower-quality sources.

AppSumo's profile says Marky came from his frustration with the grind of crafting and scheduling social posts across platforms. It says the company is based in Austin, TX and was bootstrapped from day one.
Momentum91 podcast page: he says he left a job at Tesla to build Marky, and grew it from a one-person operation to a 12-person team.
His LinkedIn profile now reads 'Deployed Eng. @ LangChain', so he may be working elsewhere now (see notes).
lessons: Distribution through a marketplace can work: a lifetime-deal platform (AppSumo) and review creators gave a young SaaS credibility and early cash. Marky's current subscription revenue comes from monthly plans.
Sell the finished output, not the tool. Marky's own pages pitch 'designs the image, not just the caption' against schedulers like Buffer.
Sell to agencies as well as end businesses: a white-label tier at $229/mo lets one agency customer bring in many client accounts.
Founder-led LinkedIn posting (launches, customer wins) is a free channel that Coad has used steadily since 2023.

Coad's own LinkedIn post says Marky spent four months building an agent inside the product, but 'should have been building for BYOA'. That is a lesson about checking where users actually work before building a big feature.
criticism: Crowded category: Buffer, Hootsuite, SocialBee, Ocoya and many AI schedulers compete. Marky's own comparison pages are marketing, not neutral.
Marky is a business for sale: TrustMRR lists it at $495,000 (2.3x revenue) with 36 buyers interested. Reasons for selling are not stated. Profit margin is hidden on TrustMRR.

Revenue is not profit. The only profit figure is the founder's listing message ($336K net income on $516K TTM). It is self-reported and was written about 110 days before today's data. Do not present it as verified.
Lifetime-deal customers bring in one-time payments, not recurring revenue. How much of Marky's base comes from AppSumo is not stated.

Reviews are mixed: Trustpilot shows mostly positive reviews plus at least one strongly negative one. One review said the AI content needs setup time and a few reviewers said it is pricey for small businesses.
Marky relies on third-party AI (OpenAI is in the stack) and on social platform APIs, so it is exposed to changes in either.
facts: TrustMRR (Stripe-verified): MRR $22,011, 476 active subscriptions, $16,664 revenue in the last 30 days, $1,015,530 all-time revenue, founded July 2023, rank #121.
The pricing page says every plan starts with 30 free posts and no credit card is needed.
A third-party comparison (onlinetoolguides.com) says Marky has 200k+ posts published across 12k channels. This is unverified.
Marky's marketing claims 3.4x more engagement than the industry average. This is Marky's own claim, not independently verified.
LinkedIn page for Marky shows only about 160 followers, so it is small. Coad's personal LinkedIn follower count is a few thousand.
do_not_claim: Do NOT name Arian Adeli as the founder. TrustMRR lists him, but every source I found names Josiah Coad as founder/CEO. Check this before naming anyone.
Do NOT say it's for self-publishing authors. TrustMRR's one-liner says that, but the product is for small businesses and agencies.
Profit or margin: only Coad's own listing message gives a profit number ($336K net income), so don't call it verified.
Team size now: '12-person team' comes from a roughly 2-year-old podcast summary.
'~200,000 users' and '30,000+ users' claims (the mymarky.com blog and TrustMRR use different numbers). Neither is verified.
Exact AppSumo sales numbers, or that AppSumo caused the growth.
The engagement claim (3.4x) and the '+340% engagement' figures from the mymarky.com review pages.
Founder X following: TrustMRR shows conflicting numbers (64 vs 1,900 followers).
Any funding. I found nothing saying it raised money, and AppSumo calls it bootstrapped.
Pricing from mymarky.com, aitools.vkweb.eu, tenereteam, onlinetoolguides ($9.99) or other third-party sites. These are outdated or wrong.
research.notes: Beware the lookalike site mymarky.com. It is a separate site, marked 'For Sale on GoDaddy', with old $97/$197/$397 pricing and '30,000+ users' claims. Don't use it. Use mymarky.ai only. The pricing page text I saw may not show the yearly price, so check the toggle on screen before saying '$19/mo billed annually' (that figure comes from the page's meta description). The AppSumo 'Tool of the Year' claim comes from third-party reviewers and a newsletter. Say 'reviewers say' or find AppSumo's own page before stating it as fact. The 1,900 vs 64 X followers for the founder on TrustMRR conflicts, so avoid follower numbers. I found no Product Hunt or Indie Hackers sources, and nothing on SEO or ads results, so the writer should not claim any growth channel beyond the sourced ones.
